messages:
hannah: Quick shout — new hires are stuck on our sample app tests. Repro uses Vitest + Vite + Edge adapter and also fails in Jenkins which uses Jest. Errors around ESM imports and jest.mock not replacing named exports.

liam: Oof. Can you paste one of the failure traces?

hannah: Short one: 
``` 
TypeError: jest.mock() failed to replace createClient
Received undefined while accessing the module's named export.
    at Object.<anonymous> (tests/client.test.ts:4:1)
Caused by: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1063:30)
```
The import in test is `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'`. The package ships ESM-only files in dist/esm and package.json has "type": "module".

mike: Two separate issues: (A) test runner can't parse ESM in node_modules (transform ignored), (B) jest.mock won't override if the module is already evaluated as ESM before mock hook runs.

tara: For Jest we tried `transformIgnorePatterns: ["/node_modules/(?!@redwood-inference/sdk)" ]` and switched to babel-jest to compile node_modules, that fixed the syntax error but mocks still weird for named exports (default import mocks worked).

liam: Named export mocking issue sometimes comes from interop: when Babel transpiles ESM -> CommonJS, named exports land on `exports.createClient`, but when Jest consumes an ESM module it may give a namespace object. The workaround is to mock the entire module as default + named entries, e.g. `jest.mock('@redwood-inference/sdk', () => ({ createClient: jest.fn(), __esModule: true }))`. Did you try __esModule flag?

hannah: Yup tried that. In Vitest the same code works with deps.inline but only if test project package.json has `type: 'module'`. Jest on Jenkins uses Node 16 and ts-jest. We also saw `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` in some runs.

mike: For ts-jest there is `useESM: true` option plus `isolatedModules`. If you flip ts-jest into ESM mode and set `extensionsToTreatAsEsm: ['.ts']` it sometimes helps. But many CI pipelines don't have vm-modules enabled, so it gets finicky.

tara: Another path: SDK team could export a tiny CJS-compatible entrypoint that re-exports the ESM implementation using createRequire. Example index.cjs: 
```js
const { createRequire } = require('module');
const requireFromEsm = createRequire(import.meta.url);
module.exports = requireFromEsm('./dist/esm/index.js');
```
That makes legacy test runners happy.

liam: Slight correction: createRequire can't require ESM files directly; you'd need a transpiled cjs build or an ESM->CJS compatibility bundle. But a small wrapper that imports the ESM and sets module.exports could be authored as a build step using rollup to produce dist/cjs.

hannah: We also noticed deep imports like `@redwood-inference/sdk/utils/serialize` pulling in ESM-only paths. We had to replace those with the public named imports to hit the exports map.

mike: For Vitest specifically: config that helped us: 
```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    environment: 'node',
    deps: { inline: ['@redwood-inference/sdk'] },
    setupFiles: ['./test/setup-vitest.js']
  },
  resolve: {
    alias: { '@redwood-inference/sdk': '/test/mocks/sdk-shim.js' }
  }
})
```
Then `sdk-shim.js` exports a CommonJS-looking interface that Vitest can mock easily.

tara: We should add a `test-utils` entry to the SDK package that re-exports minimal factories (createMockClient) meant for unit tests so teams don't rely on mocking internals. That avoids the whole ESM/CJS test-mocking friction.

hannah: Agree. For immediate onboarding unblock I put a tiny shim in repo root and pointed vite/jest aliases at it. Not ideal but unblocks folks.

liam: I'm going to open a PR template in SDK repo to include: (1) dist/cjs build, (2) exports map covering `/utils/*`, (3) `test-utils` export, (4) sample Jest & Vitest configs in `examples/testing`.

dev-tools-bot: New issue created: #412 "SDK test compatibility: ESM/CJS and mocking with Jest/Vitest" — assigned to @liam — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412

ci-bot: Jenkins: queued job #build-2097 for branch feature/tests-shim — estimated 4m

mike: Side note: people using swc-jest saw faster transforms. If we convert SDK to ship source (TS) + exports map and let app runners transpile, then swc/babel/ts-jest can correctly handle the module shape. But that shifts build burden to consumers. Probably only acceptable for OSS ecosystems.

hannah: For documentation, please include a cookbook: Vitest inline deps + alias shim, Jest transformIgnorePattern + __esModule mock example, ts-jest useESM notes, and sample manual mock for `createClient`. New hires need this in onboarding guide.

tara: Also callout Node versions and `--experimental-vm-modules` history. Add a snippet for setting `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules` in CI with a big warning about Node 18+ stable changes.

hannah: Will compile our small repro and attach to issue #412. Thanks y'all — freeing new engineers blocked on tests will help ramp. :+1:
